newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares end week up, Solidere mixed.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares end week up, Solidere mixed.

text.p: Bank shares rose on sharply reduced turnover on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday and dealers said strong demand should sustain shares.
Solidere A shares were expected to fall by $0.125 below an alltime low of $10.25, their Friday closing, unless a bloc of intervention demand picked them up on Monday, dealers said.
Banque Audi, which has performed strongly since its January 20 debut, closed at $18.25 from last week's $18. Weekly turnover in the bank shares fell to 87,914 from 216,827.
The other listed bank, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, rose to $13.125 from $12.875 on turnover of 42,025 shares from 51,748 last week.
"Bank shares are sustainable. As long as there is strong demand, they should be. If there is any correction on the Audi shares, the share should stabilise around $18," a dealer said.
Solidere shares were mixed. A shares were steady for the second week at their alltime low of $10.25 while B shares, issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994, fell to $10.625 from $10.75.
A total of 581,950 A shares were traded compared with 498,686 a week earlier.
"I expect A shares to fall on Monday by 1/8 unless there is heavy intervention to sustain the market," the dealer said.
Dealers said the A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in central Beirut -- were trading at lower prices on the grey market.
They said A shares were trading off the bourse at prices ranging between $8 and $9.5.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.27 percent on the week to 894.09 while the LISPI share index rose 0.6 percent to 82.37.
The market's total weekly turnover rose to 921,420 from 886,507 and value was $9,955,180 against $10,829,026.
Also traded were 10,000 Ciments Libanais shares at $1.15625, from 1,000 shares traded at the same price last week.
Eternit shares rose on turnover of 33,800 shares to $1.6875 from $1.625 on February 26 when they were last traded.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms: Uniceramic and Ciments Blancs.
